What is the difference between `gelu`, `gelu_new`, and `gelu_fast`?

They have subtle differences in how to approximate GELU (https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/activations.py). To my understanding, these methods can be largely divided into two categories: `nn.GELU(approximate="none")` and the other that is close to `nn.GELU(approximate="tanh")`.  `gelu_new` and `gelu_fast` belong to the second category. 

More specifically, the implementation of `gelu_new` is
```python
0.5 * input * (1.0 + torch.tanh(math.sqrt(2.0 / math.pi) * (input + 0.044715 * torch.pow(input, 3.0))))
```
while the implementation of `gelu_fast` is
```python
0.5 * input * (1.0 + torch.tanh(input * 0.7978845608 * (1.0 + 0.044715 * input * input)))
```
They are mathematically equivalent, but have small differences in approximations and the order of computation.
While using these implementations is more accurate, I chose to use `nn.GELU(tanh)` because the above implementations are very slow.

This fixes an issue when a head is to be deleted when heads have already been removed from that layer. Example:

If the layer has four heads, represented here by an 'H', the layer is of shape:
```
[H H H H]
```
If the third head (index 2) is removed: 
```
[H H X H] -> [H H H]
```
If the user tries to remove the third head in this scenario (the layer now only has three heads), he has to remove the fourth head (and not the third), because we are keeping track of the removed head. If the user tries to remove the third head, the model will raise an error because this head has already been removed.

However, when removing the fourth head, the model has to know it has shifted position and is now the third. That's why here we are counting the heads on the left side of the to-be-removed head to adjust the current head position.
